CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to assess the ongoing management of generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches, and to evaluate the effectiveness of recent medication adjustments.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith presents for his follow-up appointment, having adhered to the treatment plan discussed during his last visit. He reports a slight improvement in his anxiety levels, attributing this to the continuation of cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) and the consistent use of sertraline at 300 mg daily. He notes that he feels more equipped to manage situational anxiety, particularly in social settings, and has implemented several coping strategies learned in therapy.
Regarding his insomnia, Mr. Smith indicates that while trazodone at 100 mg at bedtime has helped with sleep initiation, nocturnal awakenings remain a significant issue, occurring approximately four to five times per night. He has increased his melatonin dosage to 20 mg as suggested, which he believes has marginally improved his sleep quality but has not resolved the awakenings. He continues to wake feeling fatigued, and he expresses frustration with this persistent issue.
His tension-type headaches have shown minimal change, maintaining a frequency of about twice weekly with a similar intensity rated between 4 and 6 out of 10. Mr. Smith reports that ibuprofen 600 mg provides satisfactory relief during headache episodes; however, he remains interested in exploring additional preventive strategies to reduce the frequency of these headaches.
Mr. Smith continues to experience persistent fatigue, which he believes is compounded by inadequate sleep and ongoing work-related stress. He notes that while bupropion at 150 mg daily has helped stabilize his energy levels to some extent, he still experiences significant afternoon lethargy and occasional difficulty concentrating.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 300 mg daily (continued) 2. Trazodone 100 mg at bedtime (continued) 3. Lisinopril 10 mg daily (continued) 4. Ibuprofen 600 mg as needed for headache relief (continued) 5. Topiramate 150 mg daily (continued) 6. Lorazepam 1 mg twice daily as needed (continued) 7. Melatonin 20 mg at bedtime (increased) 8. Modafinil 100 mg in the morning (continued) 9. Bupropion 150 mg daily (continued)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith maintains a balanced lifestyle, continuing regular physical activity such as yoga and brisk walking. He reports that he has been diligent in practicing mindfulness techniques, although work stress occasionally disrupts his routine. He has also engaged in social activities to further combat anxiety.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Anxiety levels improved; persistent sleep quality issues; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Headache frequency stable; intensity rated as moderate; no dizziness or visual disturbances noted. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue continues; no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 120/78 mmHg, HR 70 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.7F - General: Alert, oriented; appears fatigued but engaged; mood appears stable with mild anxiety. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed; no tenderness in the temporal region. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable with mild anxiety.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 300 mg daily. Maintain CBT sessions; assess progress at the next visit. Lorazepam at 1 mg twice daily as needed for acute anxiety will remain on the regimen. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone at 100 mg at bedtime. Monitor the effect of increased melatonin to 20 mg; consider further adjustments if sleep quality does not improve in the coming month. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue topiramate at 150 mg daily; maintain ibuprofen at 600 mg as needed. Discuss potential referral to a neurologist for evaluation of preventive therapies if headache frequency or intensity does not improve. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Continue bupropion at 150 mg daily; encourage regular exercise and stress management techniques. Re-evaluate fatigue levels and consider additional interventions if there is no improvement by the next appointment.
Follow-up appointment is scheduled for 2029-08-01 to continue monitoring symptom progression, medication efficacy, and address any new concerns. Mr. Smith is encouraged to keep a detailed log of his symptoms, medication responses, and any potential triggers for his anxiety or headaches to facilitate ongoing management.
